_meta.purpose: Research-backed terminology reference for mapping real bill/receipt text to canonical Policy Master expense categories. Documentation/provenance only - never loaded at runtime, never used to make network calls from the classification pipeline. The actual runtime vocabulary lives in bill_parser.py's CATEGORY_KEYWORDS (regex patterns, hand-derived from this research with additional false-positive guarding) and category_map.py's CATEGORY_TO_BILL_LABEL.
_meta.scope_note: Of the 29 canonical Policy Master categories, 4 never require a supporting document (BATTA, COMPANY CAR MAINTENANCE, OFFICE EXPENSES - DRIVER SALARY, TWO WHEELER MAINTENANCE - all document_required=DNA/NO) and so never reach category-consistency validation. Of the remaining 25, 9 already had working bill-evidence vocabulary before this research (AIRFARE, CAB CHARGES, LOCAL CONVEYANCE, LODGING, MARKETING EXPENSES - FOOD, OWN/COMPANY CAR/TWO WHEELER PETROL, PRINTING & STATIONERY, STAFF WELFARE, TRAIN / BUS FARE). This file's dedicated research covers the 16 categories/topics with a demonstrated real-world gap: 12 categories with zero bill-evidence vocabulary at all, plus targeted broadening for Fuel (brand/OCR gap), Lodging (hotel-name near-miss), and Transport Charges (mapping correction).
_meta.research_method: Each entry below was researched individually via multiple targeted web searches (not one generic query), prioritizing official vendor/provider/government documentation, Indian accounting/GST references, and established accounting-software documentation. Every item is attributed either to a cited source URL or explicitly listed under inferred_not_sourced. Entries are read-only research notes - no entry was copied verbatim into runtime regex without additional false-positive review (see bill_parser.py comments for what was actually adopted and why).

exclusion_or_conflicting_evidence: CRITICAL FALSE-POSITIVE RISK: short generic hotel-brand-suffix words - INN, SUITES, RESORT, RESIDENCY, GRAND/GRANDE, REGENCY, PALACE - must NOT be added as standalone strong-match keywords. These are proprietary brand-tier names (Hyatt Regency, Country Inn & Suites, The Residency Group) with no documented universal naming convention, and carry real collision risk: 'Inn' is a common short English word/substring, 'Grand'/'Grande' collides with 'Grand Total' on virtually every invoice, 'Palace' collides with venue/monument names, 'Suites'/'Resort' can appear on unrelated property/venue bills.

If used at all, these suffix words should only count as a WEAK secondary signal co-occurring with another weak structural hotel signal (FOLIO, TARIFF, NIGHTS, BOOKING ID, CHECK-IN/CHECK-OUT) - never alone.

A UPI/bank-transfer screenshot paid to a business whose name happens to contain one of these suffix words (confirmed real case: 'Palm Grove Suites Inn') typically carries NO other lodging-specific text at all - this is a known, currently-unsolved residual gap that keyword vocabulary cannot fully close; it would need payee-name fuzzy-matching or merchant-category-code logic instead.
Room service/restaurant items on a folio bill at restaurant GST rate, not room rate - don't let 'RESTAURANT'/'ROOM SERVICE' alone override an otherwise-clear hotel-folio classification.

'RESORT' overlaps with conference/seminar venues (often resorts/hotels) - when both seminar and hotel language appear together, the two categories may both have partial evidence and are not mutually exclusive.
